step_actions.description: Extracts, tests, or replaces text with a timeout-bounded regular expression (Regexp.timeout, 1s) so a catastrophic pattern cannot hang the run. Reads sourceVariable. Writes resultVar: a capture string, an array of scans, a boolean test, or the replaced string. Use string_manipulate for trim, case, slug, pad, and literal replace, and validate_value for a whole-value pattern check. Fails with regex_extract.failed on an invalid pattern or a timeout.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the text to search (e.g. params.invoice_number).

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Context variable that receives the match, scan list, boolean test, or replaced text.

config_fields.name: pattern
config_fields.description: Ruby regular expression source, without wrapping slashes. Example: (\d+) to capture digits. Max 4096 bytes.

config_fields.name: operation
config_fields.description: match returns one capture; scan returns every match; test writes true or false; replace substitutes every match with replacement.

config_fields.name: flags
config_fields.description: One Ruby regexp flag: none, i (ignore case), m (multiline, dot matches newline), or x (extended comments).

config_fields.name: regexFlags
config_fields.description: Combination of i, m, x, n flag letters that overrides flags when set. Example: im. Leave blank to use flags.

config_fields.name: returnType
config_fields.description: What match keeps: first is captureGroup of the first match; all is every match (like scan); named_hash is named captures as a Hash.

config_fields.name: captureGroup
config_fields.description: Capture index for returnType first. 0 is the whole match; 1 is the first parenthesis group.

config_fields.name: replacement
config_fields.description: Replacement text for replace. May include \1-style backreferences. Example: [REDACTED].

config_fields.name: fallbackValue
config_fields.description: Ruby expression written when match finds nothing (e.g. nil, "", or {}). Ignored for scan, test, and replace.

step_actions.label: Serialize Data
step_actions.description: Serializes a Hash or Array to JSON, XML, YAML, CSV, or TOML text. Reads sourceVariable. Writes resultVar as a string. CSV treats an array of hashes as rows with a header line. Use parse_data to read those formats back and format_value for a single display value. Fails with serialize_data.failed when the value cannot be represented in the chosen format.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the Hash or Array to serialize (e.g. order or line_items).

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Context variable that receives the serialized string.

config_fields.name: format
config_fields.description: Output format: json, xml, yaml, csv (array of hashes becomes a headered table), or toml.

config_fields.name: pretty
config_fields.description: Indent JSON with JSON.pretty_generate. Off writes a compact one-line object.

config_fields.name: jsonMaxDepth
config_fields.description: Maximum JSON nesting (1-100). 0 uses the JSON gem default (unlimited). Deep trees fail the step.

config_fields.name: includeRoot
config_fields.description: Keep ActiveSupport XML type attributes on elements. Off writes skip_types XML.

config_fields.name: rootElement
config_fields.description: XML root element name. Example: order. Default data.

config_fields.name: excludeNils
config_fields.description: Drop nil values with compact before serializing a Hash or Array.

step_actions.label: String Manipulate
step_actions.description: Transforms one string: strip or squish whitespace, change case, parameterize a slug, truncate, pad, split, join, replace or gsub, mask the middle for PII, HTML escape or unescape, and Base64 encode or decode. Reads sourceVariable. Writes resultVar. Use regex_extract for captures and tests, and format_value for locale display. Fails with string_manipulate.failed on an invalid gsub pattern or undecodable Base64.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the string (or array for join) to transform (e.g. params.customer_name).

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Context variable that receives the transformed string or, for split, the array of parts.

config_fields.name: operation
config_fields.description: Transform to apply. strip trims ends; squish collapses inner space; parameterize is a URL slug; mask_middle hides the middle of a PAN or ID; gsub replaces every pattern match.

config_fields.name: regexEscape
config_fields.description: Treat the gsub pattern as a literal string (Regexp.escape) instead of a regular expression.

config_fields.name: delimiter
config_fields.description: Separator for split and join. Example: , or | . Default is a comma.

config_fields.name: length
config_fields.description: Target length for pad and truncate, or how many characters to keep at each end for mask_middle. Example: 4.

config_fields.name: padChar
config_fields.description: Fill character for pad, or the mask character for mask_middle (default space; use * for cards).

config_fields.name: pattern
config_fields.description: Search text for replace (first match) or gsub (every match). Example: - or \s+.

config_fields.name: replacement
config_fields.description: Replacement text for replace and gsub. Blank deletes the matched text.

config_fields.name: urlSafe
config_fields.description: Use the URL-safe Base64 alphabet (- and _) instead of + and /.

step_actions.label: Type Cast
step_actions.description: Converts a value to a business type using ActiveModel::Type: string, integer, decimal, boolean, date, datetime, or array. Invalid integers such as 'abc' do not become 0; they fail or follow onError (fail, nil, default). Use map_value to translate enums, calculate for numeric aggregates, and parse_data for JSON text. Reads sourceVariable; writes resultVar. Fails with type_cast.failed when onError is fail and the value cannot be cast.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Ctx path of the value to cast. Example: amount or submitted_on.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable later steps read. Example: amount_cents or starts_on.

config_fields.name: targetType
config_fields.description: Type to cast to. string/integer/decimal/boolean use ActiveModel::Type; date/datetime parse in Time.zone; array wraps a value or parses a JSON list.

config_fields.name: format
config_fields.description: strftime pattern for date and datetime. Example: %Y-%m-%d. Leave blank to use Date.parse / Time.zone.parse.

config_fields.name: timezone
config_fields.description: Time zone name for datetime, e.g. UTC or America/New_York. Blank uses Time.zone.

config_fields.name: onError
config_fields.description: When the value cannot be cast: fail stops the step with type_cast.failed; nil writes nil; default writes defaultValue.

config_fields.name: defaultValue
config_fields.description: Value stored when onError is default. Example: 0 or 1970-01-01. Required for that mode.

step_actions.label: Evaluate rules
step_actions.description: Evaluates a decision table of condition/result rows with DMN-style hit policies for pricing tiers, eligibility, routing, or scoring. Use first for the first matching row, collect for every match, sum/min/max/count for numeric matches, and any when every match must return the same value. Use transition_state to move a status, or select_assignee to pick a person. Reads nothing from ctx except what the row expressions themselves read. Writes the decision value to resultVar and 1-based matched row numbers to matchedVar. Refuses evaluate_rules.no_match, non_numeric, or any_conflict.

config_fields.name: rules
config_fields.description: Decision-table rows in order. Each key is a Ruby condition over ctx (for example ctx[:amount].to_d > 1000) and each value is the result expression (for example "vip"). first stops at the first true condition; other policies collect every true row. A catch-all row uses true as the condition.

config_fields.name: hitPolicy
config_fields.description: How matching rows combine. first: first match only. collect: array of all results. sum/min/max: numeric aggregate (BigDecimal). count: how many rows matched (results are not evaluated). any: all matches must be equal, otherwise the step fails.

config_fields.name: uniqueResults
config_fields.description: When hitPolicy is collect, drop duplicate values from the result array while keeping the matched row numbers. Off (default) keeps duplicates.

config_fields.name: defaultValue
config_fields.description: Ruby expression used when nothing matches and onNoMatch is default, such as "standard" or nil. Ignored when onNoMatch is fail.

config_fields.name: onNoMatch
config_fields.description: When no rule matches: default writes defaultValue to resultVar and continues; fail refuses the run as evaluate_rules.no_match.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable later steps read for the decision result, such as rule_result. Shape depends on hitPolicy: a single value, an array (collect), or a number (sum/min/max/count).

config_fields.name: matchedVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable for the 1-based row numbers that matched, such as matched_rules. Empty array when nothing matched and onNoMatch is default.

step_actions.label: Select assignee
step_actions.description: Picks one owner or agent from a candidate pool for ticket routing and lead distribution. Load candidates yourself into sourceVariable (query_models of a staff entity, or a prior list), or set candidateSource to role to pick among this tenant's active admin or member users. Strategies: round_robin (tenant-scoped counter), least_loaded, weighted, random, first. Use transition_state to move a status after assignment. Reads sourceVariable or the tenant user list. Writes the chosen candidate or id to resultVar. Refuses select_assignee.no_candidates when the pool is empty and onEmpty is fail.

config_fields.name: candidateSource
config_fields.description: variable (default): pick from the array at sourceVariable. role: pick from this tenant's active users who have the reserved role in role (admin or member). Round-robin still uses poolKey.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Ctx path of the candidate array when candidateSource is variable, such as agents. Items may be hashes, EntityEntry records, User records, or scalar ids.

config_fields.name: role
config_fields.description: Reserved role whose active users of this customer form the pool when candidateSource is role. admin is customer administrators; member is self-signed-up members. Never includes owner.

config_fields.name: strategy
config_fields.description: How one candidate is chosen from the eligible pool. round_robin rotates a tenant-scoped counter named by poolKey. least_loaded picks the lowest loadField. weighted draws by weightField. random picks uniformly. first takes the first remaining.

config_fields.name: poolKey
config_fields.description: Tenant-scoped name of the rotation counter used by round_robin, such as support_desk. Separate keys keep independent rotations (for example billing vs support).

config_fields.name: weightField
config_fields.description: Hash or record field that holds each candidate's relative weight when strategy is weighted, such as weight. Missing or non-numeric weights count as 0.

config_fields.name: loadField
config_fields.description: Hash or record field that holds each candidate's current load when strategy is least_loaded, such as open_items. Missing or non-numeric loads count as 0.

config_fields.name: availabilityField
config_fields.description: When set, only candidates whose field is truthy (true, 1, "true") are eligible, such as available. Leave blank to include everyone.

config_fields.name: excludeVariable
config_fields.description: Optional ctx path of an id or list of ids to skip, such as previous_assignee. Compared as strings against idField. Leave blank to skip nobody.

config_fields.name: idField
config_fields.description: Hash or record field used as the candidate id, such as id. Scalar candidates use their own value. Used for exclude matching and when returns is id.

config_fields.name: returns
config_fields.description: candidate (default) stores the whole chosen item on resultVar. id stores only the value of idField (or the scalar itself).

config_fields.name: onEmpty
config_fields.description: When no eligible candidate remains: fail refuses the run as select_assignee.no_candidates; nil stores nil on resultVar and continues.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable later steps read for the chosen assignee, such as assignee. A whole candidate or an id according to returns.

step_actions.label: Transition state
step_actions.description: Moves a record field or ctx variable through a declared state machine and rejects transitions the map does not allow. On a page record, leave transitions empty to follow that status field's Entities::Lifecycle (any of its transitions; Entries::Save still checks who may). Use request_payment paidFields for a status a payment confirms, never this step. Reads modelVariable/stateField or stateVariable, plus targetState or targetVariable. Writes resultVar, previousStateVar, and transitionedVar. Does not save the record. Refuses transition_state.invalid_transition, guard_failed, or missing_record.

config_fields.name: stateSource
config_fields.description: record (default) reads and writes a field on the loaded EntityEntry at modelVariable. variable reads and writes a plain ctx variable named by stateVariable (not a nested path).

config_fields.name: modelVariable
config_fields.description: Ctx path of the loaded EntityEntry, such as model. The field is written in memory only; a later save_model persists it.

config_fields.name: stateField
config_fields.description: Attribute slug that holds the current state, such as status. Must be a writable field of that record's entity. The record is not saved by this step.

config_fields.name: stateVariable
config_fields.description: Plain ctx variable name that holds the current state, such as status. Nested paths (order.status) are rejected because the new state could not be written back.

config_fields.name: targetSource
config_fields.description: literal uses targetState. variable reads the next state from targetVariable at runtime (for example a decision-table result).

config_fields.name: targetState
config_fields.description: State to move to when the map or lifecycle allows it, such as approved. Must match an option value of the status field, not its label.

config_fields.name: targetVariable
config_fields.description: Ctx path of the state to move to when targetSource is variable, such as next_status. Evaluated at runtime.

config_fields.name: transitions
config_fields.description: From-state mapped to allowed targets. Each value is one slug or a comma-separated list (approved, rejected). Use * as the from-state to allow any current state. Leave empty on a record step to follow the field's lifecycle.

config_fields.name: initialState
config_fields.description: State assumed when the current value is blank, such as draft. On a lifecycle-backed record step, the field's default option is used when this is blank.

config_fields.name: allowSameState
config_fields.description: When on, a target equal to the current state is a successful no-op (transitionedVar is false, state unchanged). Off (default) treats it as invalid unless the map lists it.

config_fields.name: guardExpression
config_fields.description: Optional extra Ruby boolean that must be true for the transition to proceed, such as ctx[:allowed]. A false guard refuses as transition_state.guard_failed (or skips when onInvalid is skip).

config_fields.name: onInvalid
config_fields.description: When the map, lifecycle, or guard rejects the transition: fail refuses the run; skip leaves the state unchanged, sets transitionedVar to false, and continues.

config_fields.name: timestampField
config_fields.description: Optional attribute stamped with Time.current when the transition happens, such as status_changed_at. The record is not saved. Leave blank to skip.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable later steps read for the resulting state, such as state. Unchanged when the step skips an invalid transition.

config_fields.name: previousStateVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable later steps read for the state before this step, such as previous_state.

config_fields.name: transitionedVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable later steps read for whether the state changed (true or false), such as transitioned.

step_actions.label: Allocate Amount
step_actions.description: Splits a money amount into parts that always sum exactly to the rounded input, using largest-remainder (Hamilton) so leftover cents are assigned and the parts add up. Use this to split an invoice across cost centres, a payment across line items, or a budget across departments. Use calculate_pricing to total an order first, or build_installment_plan for a repayment schedule. Reads amount, and weightsVariable when method is ratio or percent. Writes the decimal-string array to resultVar. Refuses allocate_amount.invalid_amount, invalid_weights, or percent_total when percent weights do not sum to 100.

config_fields.name: amount
config_fields.description: Ctx path of the amount to split, such as total or invoice.grand_total. Must evaluate to a number (integer, decimal string, or BigDecimal).

config_fields.name: method
config_fields.description: even splits into equal parts (set parts). ratio splits by relative weights from weightsVariable. percent is ratio but the weights must sum to 100.

config_fields.name: parts
config_fields.description: How many equal parts to create when method is even, from 1 to 1000. Ignored for ratio and percent, where the weights list length is the part count.

config_fields.name: weightsVariable
config_fields.description: Ctx path of the weights array when method is ratio or percent, such as weights. Each item is a number, or a hash/record whose weight is read from weightField.

config_fields.name: weightField
config_fields.description: Hash or record key to read when weights are objects, such as share. Leave blank to try weight, value, ratio, percent, then share in that order.

config_fields.name: precision
config_fields.description: Decimal places for each allocated amount (0-6). Use 2 for CNY/USD. Parts are rounded to this scale then adjusted so they still sum to the input.

config_fields.name: remainderStrategy
config_fields.description: Where leftover units go after rounding so parts still sum to the input. largest_remainder (default, Hamilton) gives extras to the largest fractional remainders; first/last give them to the first or last parts; largest_share gives them to the biggest weights.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable that receives the array of allocated amounts as decimal strings at the chosen precision, such as allocations. Example: ["33.34", "33.33", "33.33"].

step_actions.label: Build Installment Plan
step_actions.description: Builds a repayment, subscription, or instalment schedule from a principal, annual rate, period count, and frequency. Use annuity for equal payments each period (standard amortizing / equal-instalment loans) and equal_principal for equal principal with declining interest (common bank loans). Use allocate_amount to split one amount, or calculate_pricing to total an order first. Reads principal (and optional rateVariable, startDateVariable). Writes the schedule array to resultVar and payment/principal/interest totals to totalsVar. Refuses invalid_principal, invalid_periods, invalid_start_date, or down_payment_exceeds_principal.

config_fields.name: principal
config_fields.description: Ctx path of the principal to finance, such as loan_amount or order.total. Must be a number greater than zero. Down payment is subtracted first.

config_fields.name: annualRate
config_fields.description: Nominal annual interest rate as a percent, such as 12 for 12 percent. Overridden at runtime when rateVariable is set. 0 means an interest-free schedule.

config_fields.name: rateVariable
config_fields.description: Optional ctx path whose numeric percent overrides annualRate at runtime, such as interest_rate from a looked-up product. Leave blank to use annualRate.

config_fields.name: periods
config_fields.description: Number of payments in the schedule, from 1 to 600. 12 with monthly frequency is one year.

config_fields.name: frequency
config_fields.description: Spacing between due dates, and the divisor that turns the annual rate into a period rate. monthly (12), quarterly (4), semiannual (2), annual (1), weekly (52), biweekly (26).

config_fields.name: method
config_fields.description: annuity: equal payment each period (PMT / equal instalment). equal_principal: equal principal each period, interest declines. interest_only: interest each period, principal balloons on the last. flat: interest charged on the original principal every period.

config_fields.name: startDateVariable
config_fields.description: Optional ctx path of the schedule origin date, such as start_date. Accepts a Date, Time, or ISO8601 date string. Blank means today in the application time zone.

config_fields.name: firstPaymentOffset
config_fields.description: How many frequency periods after the start date the first instalment is due. 1 (default) is next period; 0 means due on the start date.

config_fields.name: downPayment
config_fields.description: Amount subtracted from principal before the schedule is built, such as 2000. Must be less than principal or the step refuses.

config_fields.name: precision
config_fields.description: Decimal places for every amount on the schedule (0-6). Use 2 for CNY/USD.

config_fields.name: roundingMode
config_fields.description: How each amount is rounded at the chosen precision. half_up is ordinary rounding; half_even is banker's rounding; floor/ceiling always go down/up.

config_fields.name: finalPaymentAdjust
config_fields.description: When on (default), the last row absorbs rounding residue so principal sums exactly to the financed amount. Turn off only when you must keep a fixed formula payment on the last row.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable for the schedule array. Each row has number, due_date (ISO8601 YYYY-MM-DD), and payment/principal/interest/balance as decimal strings.

config_fields.name: totalsVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable for the payment, principal, and interest totals as decimal strings at the chosen precision, such as installment_totals.

step_actions.label: Calculate Pricing
step_actions.description: Totals an order, invoice, or quote from line items. Order of operations is fixed: line gross (quantity times unit price), minus per-line discount, then order-level discount split across remaining line nets with largest remainder (never below zero), then tax, then shipping. Exclusive tax adds on payable; inclusive extracts tax from the entered price; none skips tax. Use request_payment to charge the total, or allocate_amount to split it. Reads sourceVariable. Writes the pricing hash (lines, subtotal, discount, tax, shipping, total, currency) to resultVar as decimal strings. Refuses calculate_pricing.invalid_line for a non-numeric or negative quantity or unit price.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Ctx path of the line-item array, such as line_items. Each item is a hash or EntityEntry with quantity and unit-price keys. A single hash or record is treated as one line.

config_fields.name: quantityField
config_fields.description: Key read from each line for quantity, such as quantity. Must be a non-negative number.

config_fields.name: unitPriceField
config_fields.description: Key read from each line for unit price, such as unit_price. Must be a non-negative number. Entered in the same units as tax, discount, and shipping.

config_fields.name: lineDiscountField
config_fields.description: Optional key for a per-line discount amount, such as line_discount. Applied before the order-level discount. Leave blank to skip. Capped so a line cannot go below zero.

config_fields.name: lineTaxRateField
config_fields.description: Optional key for a per-line tax-rate percent that overrides taxRate, such as tax_rate. Leave blank to use the order tax rate on every line.

config_fields.name: discountType
config_fields.description: Order-level discount applied after line discounts. none skips it. percent takes discountValue as 0-100 of remaining line nets. amount takes discountValue as a money amount split across lines pro rata (largest remainder) and never pushes a line below zero.

config_fields.name: discountValue
config_fields.description: Percent (0-100) or money amount according to discountType, such as 10. Overridden at runtime when discountVariable is set. Ignored when discountType is none.

config_fields.name: discountVariable
config_fields.description: Optional ctx path whose numeric value overrides discountValue at runtime, such as coupon_amount from a redeemed coupon. Leave blank to use discountValue.

config_fields.name: taxMode
config_fields.description: When tax is applied, after discounts. exclusive adds tax on top of payable (net x rate). inclusive extracts tax from the entered payable (price already includes tax). none skips tax and shippingTaxable.

config_fields.name: taxRate
config_fields.description: Order-level tax rate as a percent (0-100), such as 13 for 13 percent VAT. A line tax-rate field overrides this per line. Ignored when taxMode is none.

config_fields.name: shippingAmount
config_fields.description: Shipping amount added after tax on merchandise, in the same units as line prices, such as 10. Overridden at runtime when shippingVariable is set. 0 means no shipping.

config_fields.name: shippingVariable
config_fields.description: Optional ctx path whose numeric value overrides shippingAmount at runtime, such as shipping from a rate lookup. Leave blank to use shippingAmount.

config_fields.name: shippingTaxable
config_fields.description: When on, shipping is taxed with the order taxRate and taxMode (exclusive adds tax on shipping; inclusive treats shippingAmount as tax-inclusive). Off (default) leaves shipping untaxed.

config_fields.name: precision
config_fields.description: Decimal places for every amount (0-6). Use 2 for CNY/USD. Combined with roundPer to decide whether each line or only the order totals are rounded.

config_fields.name: roundingMode
config_fields.description: How amounts are rounded at the chosen precision. half_up is ordinary rounding; half_even is banker's rounding; floor/ceiling always go down/up.

config_fields.name: roundPer
config_fields.description: line (default) rounds each line's net/tax/total then sums. total keeps line math exact and rounds only the order subtotal, discount, tax, shipping, and total.

config_fields.name: currency
config_fields.description: Optional ISO 4217 code echoed into the result, such as CNY. Not used for conversion or rounding; set it so later steps (request_payment) can read pricing.currency.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable for the pricing hash. Amounts are decimal strings at the chosen precision (for example "10.00"). Keys: lines, subtotal, discount, tax, shipping, total, currency.

step_actions.label: HTTP request
step_actions.description: Calls an external HTTP API and stores the response. Use send_webhook for a signed POST to a subscriber URL, or send_chat_message for Slack/Teams/DingTalk/WeCom/Feishu incoming webhooks. Reads url, optional queryParams, headers, bodyTemplate (POST/PUT/PATCH), and authType credentials from ctx/ENV expressions (never paste secrets). Writes resultVar (default api_response): parsed JSON, text, or raw bytes. Optionally writes statusVar and headersVar. Fails on blocked destinations, transport errors, non-2xx when failOnHttpError is true, or invalid JSON when responseFormat is json.

config_fields.name: httpMethod
config_fields.description: HTTP verb. GET/HEAD/OPTIONS send no body. POST/PUT/PATCH send bodyTemplate encoded as bodyFormat. DELETE has no body. Default GET.

config_fields.name: url
config_fields.description: Request URL as Ruby, e.g. "https://api.example.com/orders" or ctx[:endpoint]. Must be a public https URL; private hosts are blocked.

config_fields.name: headers
config_fields.description: Extra header name to value. Static text, or a ctx/ENV expression such as ctx[:request_id]. Authorization is set by authType, not here.

config_fields.name: queryParams
config_fields.description: Query string keys appended to the URL. Values are static text or a ctx/ENV expression such as ctx[:order_id].

config_fields.name: bodyTemplate
config_fields.description: Ruby expression for the POST/PUT/PATCH body, e.g. ctx[:payload] or { id: ctx[:order_id] }. Hidden for GET/HEAD/DELETE/OPTIONS.

config_fields.name: bodyFormat
config_fields.description: How bodyTemplate is encoded: json (.to_json), form (form:), text/xml/binary (raw string). Sets Content-Type except form. Default json.

config_fields.name: authType
config_fields.description: none sends no credentials. bearer sets Authorization: Bearer <authToken>. basic sets Basic auth from authUsername/authPassword. apiKey sets apiKeyHeader.

config_fields.name: authToken
config_fields.description: Bearer token or API key as a ctx/ENV/credentials expression, e.g. ENV.fetch("API_TOKEN", nil). Never a quoted secret string.

config_fields.name: authUsername
config_fields.description: Basic-auth username expression, e.g. ENV.fetch("API_USER", nil).

config_fields.name: authPassword
config_fields.description: Basic-auth password expression, e.g. ENV.fetch("API_PASSWORD", nil). Never a quoted secret string.

config_fields.name: apiKeyHeader
config_fields.description: Header that carries the API key when authType is apiKey. Default X-API-Key.

config_fields.name: responseFormat
config_fields.description: How the body is stored in resultVar: json (parsed object, {} if empty), text (string), or binary (raw bytes). Default json. Invalid JSON fails the step.

config_fields.name: responseParseKey
config_fields.description: Optional dotted JSON path kept from the parsed object, e.g. data.user. Blank stores the whole object. Ignored unless responseFormat is json.

config_fields.name: followRedirects
config_fields.description: Follow HTTP redirects up to maxRedirects hops. Default true.

config_fields.name: maxRedirects
config_fields.description: Maximum redirect hops when followRedirects is true (0-20). Default 5.

config_fields.name: failOnHttpError
config_fields.description: When true (default), a non-2xx response fails the step with http_status. When false, the body is still stored so a later step can branch on statusVar.

config_fields.name: idempotencyKey
config_fields.description: Value sent as Idempotency-Key. Also allows transport retry on POST/PATCH when retryOnTransportError is on. Example: ctx[:request_id].

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: ctx key for the parsed body (default api_response). Later steps read this hash, string, or bytes.

config_fields.name: statusVar
config_fields.description: Optional ctx key that stores the HTTP status code, e.g. http_status. Blank skips it.

config_fields.name: headersVar
config_fields.description: Optional ctx key that stores response headers, e.g. http_headers. Blank skips it.

config_fields.name: retryOnTransportError
config_fields.description: Retry once more when the connection fails before any response arrives. Allowed only for idempotent requests, so a retried call cannot act twice.

config_fields.name: retryAttempts
config_fields.description: Extra attempts after a transport failure (1-2) when retryOnTransportError is on.

config_fields.name: connectTimeout
config_fields.description: Seconds to wait for the connection to open (1-5). connectTimeout + readTimeout must stay within 10 seconds.

config_fields.name: readTimeout
config_fields.description: Seconds to wait for the response once connected (1-9); a slower answer fails the step.

config_fields.name: circuitBreaker
config_fields.description: Stop calling the remote service for a while after repeated failures, failing fast instead of waiting on every run.

config_fields.name: breakerName
config_fields.description: Name of the breaker; steps that call the same service share one name so they trip together.

config_fields.name: failureThreshold
config_fields.description: Consecutive failures that open the breaker (1-20).

config_fields.name: resetTimeoutSeconds
config_fields.description: Seconds the breaker stays open before one trial call is let through (10-3600).

step_actions.label: Create notification
step_actions.description: Creates an in-app notification for one or more users of this customer. Use send_email to send mail, and load_current_user when you need the signed-in user's email or role first. recipient is a Ruby expression for a user id (default ctx[:current_user_id]); recipients lists extra ctx paths of user ids. title and body are localized hashes stored as written. page is an optional launched same-customer or shared page stored as the link. Writes one row per distinct same-tenant user. Fails as recipient_not_found when any id is missing or foreign, page_not_found when page is set but not launched, or create_notification.failed when customer_id is missing.

config_fields.name: recipient
config_fields.description: Ruby expression for a user id of this customer, or an array of ids. Default ctx[:current_user_id] is the signed-in account, not a person record id.

config_fields.name: recipients
config_fields.description: Extra ctx paths of user ids to notify, such as admin_id or owner.id. Combined with recipient; duplicates are notified once.

config_fields.name: title
config_fields.description: Localized notification title as {"en" => "Order received", "zh-CN" => "..."}. Stored as written; it is not interpolated.

config_fields.name: body
config_fields.description: Localized notification body as a locale-key hash. Stored as written; put any order number in the text yourself.

config_fields.name: page
config_fields.description: Optional launched page of this customer, or a shared page, stored as the notification link. A draft, missing, or other-tenant page fails the step.

step_actions.label: Send Chat Message
step_actions.description: Posts text or Markdown to a Slack, Teams, DingTalk, WeCom, or Feishu incoming webhook. Use send_webhook for a generic signed POST, or send_email for email. Reads provider, webhookUrl, messageType, text (Liquid), optional title (Markdown), mentionAll, mentionMobiles (DingTalk/WeCom), and signingSecret (DingTalk/Feishu). Writes resultVar (default chat_response) with the parsed provider body. Fails with send_chat_message.delivery_failed, provider_error, transport_failed, or render_failed.

config_fields.name: provider
config_fields.description: Chat platform that owns the incoming webhook: slack (default), teams, dingtalk, wecom, or feishu.

config_fields.name: webhookUrl
config_fields.description: Incoming webhook URL as Ruby, e.g. "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T../B../...". Must be a public https URL.

config_fields.name: messageType
config_fields.description: text (default) sends a plain body. markdown sends a formatted payload and shows the title field.

config_fields.name: title
config_fields.description: Optional heading above a Markdown message, e.g. New order {{ order_number }}. Hidden when messageType is text.

config_fields.name: text
config_fields.description: Message body. Liquid placeholders resolve from ctx, e.g. New order {{ order_number }}.

config_fields.name: mentionAll
config_fields.description: When true, pings every member (@channel / @all). Default false.

config_fields.name: mentionMobiles
config_fields.description: Mobile numbers @-mentioned on DingTalk or WeCom, e.g. 13800138000. Hidden for other providers.

config_fields.name: signingSecret
config_fields.description: DingTalk or Feishu bot signing secret as a ctx/ENV expression, e.g. ENV.fetch("CHAT_SECRET", nil). Never a quoted secret. Hidden for other providers.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: ctx key for the parsed provider response (default chat_response). JSON object, or {body:} when the remote returns non-JSON text.

config_fields.name: connectTimeout
config_fields.description: Seconds to wait for the connection to open (1-5). connectTimeout + readTimeout must stay within 10 seconds.

config_fields.name: readTimeout
config_fields.description: Seconds to wait for the response once connected (1-9); a slower answer fails the step.

config_fields.name: circuitBreaker
config_fields.description: Stop calling the remote service for a while after repeated failures, failing fast instead of waiting on every run.

config_fields.name: breakerName
config_fields.description: Name of the breaker; steps that call the same service share one name so they trip together.

config_fields.name: failureThreshold
config_fields.description: Consecutive failures that open the breaker (1-20).

config_fields.name: resetTimeoutSeconds
config_fields.description: Seconds the breaker stays open before one trial call is let through (10-3600).

step_actions.label: Send Email
step_actions.description: Sends an email whose To, subject and body are written on this step (Liquid from ctx). Use send_template_email when the admin named an Emails template instead. Reads to/cc/bcc/replyTo templates, optional attachmentsVariable (a generate_document result, a generate_file or download_file file, a record's File or Image field, or blob ids), locale, and idempotencyKey. Delivers through Emails::Gateway.send_raw for ctx[:customer_id]. Writes resultVar (default email_message_ids) with ledger ids. onError continue (default) keeps the submission if delivery cannot start; fail refuses it with send_email.failed.

config_fields.name: to
config_fields.description: Recipient addresses, comma/semicolon/space separated. May read the record, e.g. {{ model.email }} or sales@example.com.

config_fields.name: subject
config_fields.description: Subject line. Record values go in {{ }}, e.g. New order {{ model.order_number }}.

config_fields.name: body
config_fields.description:
Plain-text body. {{ }} placeholders resolve from ctx. HTML is escaped; newlines become
.

config_fields.name: cc
config_fields.description: Carbon-copy addresses, same format as to. Blank sends no CC. Example: manager@example.com.

config_fields.name: bcc
config_fields.description: Blind carbon-copy addresses, same format as to. Blank sends no BCC. Example: audit@example.com.

config_fields.name: replyTo
config_fields.description: Reply-To address. Blank uses the Email module From address. Example: support@example.com.

config_fields.name: locale
config_fields.description: I18n locale while sending, e.g. "zh-CN" or ctx[:locale]. Blank uses ctx[:locale] or I18n.locale.

config_fields.name: attachmentsVariable
config_fields.description: ctx path of a generate_document result (blob_id hash), a generate_file or download_file file ({filename, content, content_type}), a record's File or Image field such as model.contract, an array of those, or blob ids. Blank sends no files.

config_fields.name: idempotencyKey
config_fields.description: Optional Emails ledger idempotency key, e.g. ctx[:request_id]. Duplicate keys reuse the existing message.

config_fields.name: onError
config_fields.description: continue (default) keeps the submission if the email cannot go out. fail refuses the submission with send_email.failed.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: ctx key for the array of Emails::Message ids (default email_message_ids). Empty array when onError is continue and send failed.

step_actions.label: Send SMS
step_actions.description: Sends an SMS through an approved customer template (no free-text body; carriers require templates). Reads templateKey, to (ctx path, default model.phone), vars, and optional idempotencyKey. Writes resultVar (default sms_message_id) with the tenant ledger id. Fails with send_sms.suppressed, quota, invalid_number, template_missing, invalid_vars, credentials_missing, module_disabled, idempotency_conflict, marketing_ineligible, provider_code_missing, api_error, or failed. Tenant-scoped to ctx[:customer_id].

config_fields.name: templateKey
config_fields.description: Approved SMS template key for this customer, e.g. verify_code. Free-text bodies are not sent.

config_fields.name: to
config_fields.description: ctx path of the recipient E.164 phone number, e.g. model.phone or user.mobile. Default model.phone.

config_fields.name: vars
config_fields.description: Template variable name to Ruby expression, e.g. code => ctx[:otp] or minutes => "5".

config_fields.name: idempotencyKey
config_fields.description: Optional SMS ledger idempotency key, e.g. ctx[:request_id]. Duplicate keys with different payloads fail with send_sms.idempotency_conflict.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: ctx key for the Sms::Message id (default sms_message_id). Later steps read this integer.

step_actions.label: Send Template Email
step_actions.description: Sends a named Emails template for this customer. Use send_email when the subject and body are written on the step instead. Reads templateId, to (ctx path of the address), vars, optional cc/bcc/replyTo, locale (default ctx[:locale] or I18n.locale), and idempotencyKey. Writes resultVar (default email_message_id) with the ledger id. Fails with send_template_email.failed when the Email module rejects the send (missing template, credentials, or invalid vars).

config_fields.name: templateId
config_fields.description: Emails template id for this customer. Pick the template the admin named; do not compose subject/body here.

config_fields.name: to
config_fields.description: ctx path of the recipient address, e.g. user.email or model.email. A member-owned record field is typical.

config_fields.name: vars
config_fields.description: Template variable name to value. Static text, a number, or a ctx/ENV expression such as ctx[:user_name].

config_fields.name: cc
config_fields.description: Optional CC address expression, e.g. ctx[:manager_email] or "ops@example.com". Blank sends no CC.

config_fields.name: bcc
config_fields.description: Optional BCC address expression, e.g. ctx[:auditor_email]. Blank sends no BCC.

config_fields.name: replyTo
config_fields.description: Optional Reply-To address expression, e.g. "support@example.com". Blank uses the Email module From.

config_fields.name: locale
config_fields.description: I18n locale while rendering and sending, e.g. "zh-CN" or ctx[:locale]. Blank uses ctx[:locale] or I18n.locale.

config_fields.name: idempotencyKey
config_fields.description: Optional Emails ledger idempotency key, e.g. ctx[:request_id]. Duplicate keys reuse the existing message.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: ctx key for the Emails::Message id (default email_message_id). Later steps read this integer.

step_actions.label: Send Webhook
step_actions.description: POSTs a JSON or form payload to a subscriber URL, optionally HMAC-signing the body. Use api_call for GET/PUT/PATCH or response parsing, and send_chat_message for chat incoming webhooks. Reads url, payloadExpression, headers, optional secretExpression (HMAC via OpenSSL), hmacAlgorithm, signatureHeader, idempotencyKey (Idempotency-Key plus transport retry), and contentType. Writes resultVar (default webhook_response) from the body (JSON object, or {body:} when the response is not JSON) and optional statusVar. Fails on transport errors, blocked destinations, non-2xx when failOnHttpError is true, or HMAC errors when signing.

config_fields.name: url
config_fields.description: Webhook URL as Ruby, e.g. "https://hooks.example.com/orders". Must be a public https URL.

config_fields.name: payloadExpression
config_fields.description: Ruby hash (or form pairs) that becomes the body, e.g. ctx[:webhook_payload] or { event: "created", id: ctx[:order_id] }.

config_fields.name: headers
config_fields.description: Extra header name to value. Static text, or a ctx/ENV expression such as ctx[:request_id]. Content-Type is set from contentType.

config_fields.name: secretExpression
config_fields.description: HMAC signing secret as a ctx/ENV/credentials expression, e.g. ENV.fetch("WEBHOOK_SECRET", nil). Blank skips signing. Never a quoted secret.

config_fields.name: hmacAlgorithm
config_fields.description: HMAC digest when secretExpression is set: sha256 (default), sha512, or sha1. Ignored when not signing.

config_fields.name: signatureHeader
config_fields.description: Header that carries the HMAC, e.g. X-Signature or X-Hub-Signature-256. Default X-Signature. Ignored when not signing.

config_fields.name: idempotencyKey
config_fields.description: Value sent as Idempotency-Key. Required to retry this POST when retryOnTransportError is on. Example: ctx[:request_id].

config_fields.name: contentType
config_fields.description: Body encoding: application/json (.to_json, default) or application/x-www-form-urlencoded (URI.encode_www_form).

config_fields.name: failOnHttpError
config_fields.description: When true (default), a non-2xx response fails the step with http_status. When false, the body is still stored so a later step can branch on statusVar.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: ctx key for the parsed body (default webhook_response). JSON object, {} if empty, or {body:} when the remote returns non-JSON text such as ok.

config_fields.name: statusVar
config_fields.description: Optional ctx key that stores the HTTP status code, e.g. hook_status. Blank skips it.

config_fields.name: retryOnTransportError
config_fields.description: Retry once more when the connection fails before any response arrives. Allowed only for idempotent requests, so a retried call cannot act twice.

config_fields.name: retryAttempts
config_fields.description: Extra attempts after a transport failure (1-2) when retryOnTransportError is on.

config_fields.name: connectTimeout
config_fields.description: Seconds to wait for the connection to open (1-5). connectTimeout + readTimeout must stay within 10 seconds.

config_fields.name: readTimeout
config_fields.description: Seconds to wait for the response once connected (1-9); a slower answer fails the step.

config_fields.name: circuitBreaker
config_fields.description: Stop calling the remote service for a while after repeated failures, failing fast instead of waiting on every run.

config_fields.name: breakerName
config_fields.description: Name of the breaker; steps that call the same service share one name so they trip together.

config_fields.name: failureThreshold
config_fields.description: Consecutive failures that open the breaker (1-20).

config_fields.name: resetTimeoutSeconds
config_fields.description: Seconds the breaker stays open before one trial call is let through (10-3600).

step_actions.label: Authenticate
step_actions.description: Verifies a password, HTTP token, API key, or the signed-in session and writes the principal (or compared secret) to resultVar. Use password after loading a tenant User; session after Load current user; token/api_key for constant-time secret compare. Use verify_token for JWTs or signed links, and authorize for role or record-owner checks. Fails with authenticate.failed unless onFailure is flag.

config_fields.name: authMethod
config_fields.description: How to authenticate. password: Devise/has_secure_password on userVariable. token: strip Bearer/Basic then compare to expectedKeyVariable. api_key: compare the raw secret. session: the Warden principal in ctx[:authentication]. Not JWT; use verify_token for that.

config_fields.name: credentialSource
config_fields.description: Where the submitted secret is read. ctx: sourceVariable on the runtime hash (e.g. credentials). params: FlowchartRuntime::Step.dig(ctx[:params], sourceVariable), e.g. params key Authorization.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Context path or params key holding the submitted password, token, or API key. Example: credentials or Authorization. Required for password, token, and api_key.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key written on success: the User for password/session, the stripped token string for token, true for api_key. Nil on failure when onFailure is flag.

config_fields.name: userVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the Authentication::User whose password is checked (has_secure_password). Example: user. Must already belong to ctx[:customer_id].

config_fields.name: tokenType
config_fields.description: Prefix stripped before constant-time compare. bearer drops 'Bearer ', basic drops 'Basic ', custom compares the raw string to expectedKeyVariable.

config_fields.name: expectedKeyVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the expected secret, e.g. stored_key. Compared in constant time. Required for token and api_key. Never paste the secret into the flowchart.

config_fields.name: onFailure
config_fields.description: fail: Step.fail authenticate.failed and stop. flag: write resultVar (possibly nil) and continue so a later decision can branch.

step_actions.label: Authorize
step_actions.description: Allows the step to continue only when the actor has a reserved role, a CanCanCan ability, any listed reserved role, or owns the record (user_id). Reads userExpression (default current_user). Use authenticate first to prove identity. Roles are only owner, admin, and member; record_owner is the member-owns-this-row check. Denied writes authorize.denied unless onDenied is flag (then resultVar is boolean).

config_fields.name: authType
config_fields.description: How this step decides. role_check: user must have roleName. multi_role: user must have any role in roleList (owner/admin/member). ability_check: CanCanCan can?(abilityAction, abilityResource) plus tenant match. record_owner: the record's user_id must equal the user's id in this tenant.

config_fields.name: userExpression
config_fields.description: Context path of the Authentication::User. Default current_user (written by Load current user). Falls back to the Warden session when the value is not a User.

config_fields.name: roleName
config_fields.description: Reserved role required for role_check. owner, admin, or member only. Default admin. A user has exactly one reserved role.

config_fields.name: abilityAction
config_fields.description: CanCanCan action name, e.g. read or update. Letters, digits, and underscores only. Required for ability_check.

config_fields.name: abilityResource
config_fields.description: Context path of the subject passed to CanCanCan, e.g. record. Another tenant's row is denied even for an admin. Required for ability_check.

config_fields.name: recordVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the EntityEntry (or hash with user_id) the member must own, e.g. model. Admin/owner do not auto-pass; use role_check for staff.

config_fields.name: roleList
config_fields.description: Reserved roles; the user may hold any one of them. Values must be owner, admin, or member. Example: admin, member. Required for multi_role.

config_fields.name: onDenied
config_fields.description: fail: stop with authorize.denied or deniedMessage. flag: write resultVar true/false and continue so a later decision can branch.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key set to true or false when onDenied is flag. Example: authorized.

config_fields.name: deniedMessage
config_fields.description: Optional localized hash {en, zh-CN} shown instead of authorize.denied when onDenied is fail. Leave blank to use the default translation.

step_actions.label: Decrypt Data
step_actions.description: Decrypts sourceVariable ciphertext produced by encrypt_data (aes-256-gcm MessageEncryptor) and writes plaintext to resultVar. keySource, keyPath, encoding, and purpose must match the encrypt step. Keys come from credentials, ENV, ctx, or a tenant-salted derived passphrase. Fails with decrypt_data.failed on a wrong key, purpose, or encoding.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the ciphertext string, e.g. encrypted. Same encoding as encrypt_data.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key that receives the plaintext string. Default decrypted.

config_fields.name: keySource
config_fields.description: Where the key is read. Must match encrypt_data: credentials (keyPath or secret_key_base), env, ctx, or derived from deriveKeyFrom plus the tenant salt.

config_fields.name: keyPath
config_fields.description: credentials: dot path such as security.primary_key. env: ENV name such as APP_DECRYPT_KEY. ctx: identifier such as cipher_key. Required for env and ctx.

config_fields.name: deriveKeyFrom
config_fields.description: Context path of the passphrase used to derive the key, e.g. master_secret. Required when keySource is derived.

config_fields.name: deriveKeySalt
config_fields.description: Extra salt mixed with customer_id as flowchart.cipher.<id>.<suffix>. Example: user_data_v1. Must match encrypt_data.

config_fields.name: encoding
config_fields.description: How the stored ciphertext is encoded. Must match encrypt_data: base64 (default), base64url, hex, or raw.

config_fields.name: purpose
config_fields.description: MessageEncryptor purpose string. Must match encrypt_data, e.g. flowchart_data or user_data. A mismatch fails the step.

step_actions.label: Encrypt Data
step_actions.description: Encrypts sourceVariable with ActiveSupport::MessageEncryptor (aes-256-gcm) and writes the ciphertext to resultVar. Pair with decrypt_data using the same keySource, keyPath, encoding, and purpose. Keys come from Rails credentials, ENV, ctx, or a tenant-salted derived passphrase — never an inline secret. Fails with encrypt_data.failed on Cipher::Error.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the plaintext string to encrypt, e.g. sensitive_data or ssn.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key that receives the encoded ciphertext. Default encrypted. Pass this path to decrypt_data as sourceVariable.

config_fields.name: keySource
config_fields.description: Where the 32-byte key is read. credentials: Rails credentials at keyPath, or secret_key_base when keyPath is blank. env: ENV[keyPath]. ctx: ctx[keyPath]. derived: PBKDF2 from deriveKeyFrom plus a tenant salt.

config_fields.name: keyPath
config_fields.description: credentials: dot path such as security.primary_key. env: ENV name such as APP_ENCRYPT_KEY. ctx: identifier such as cipher_key. Required for env and ctx.

config_fields.name: deriveKeyFrom
config_fields.description: Context path of the passphrase used to derive the key, e.g. master_secret. Required when keySource is derived.

config_fields.name: deriveKeySalt
config_fields.description: Extra salt mixed with customer_id as flowchart.cipher.<id>.<suffix>. Example: user_data_v1. Must match decrypt_data.

config_fields.name: encoding
config_fields.description: How the ciphertext is stored. base64 (default) for JSON/text columns, base64url for URLs, hex for hex columns, raw for binary columns. Decrypt must use the same.

config_fields.name: purpose
config_fields.description: MessageEncryptor purpose string. Encrypt and decrypt must share it, e.g. flowchart_data or user_data. A mismatch refuses to decrypt.

step_actions.label: Generate Token
step_actions.description: Issues a JWT (jwt gem, HS256/HS384/HS512/RS256), a Rails MessageVerifier signed payload, or a numeric OTP and writes it to resultVar. Use verify_token to check JWT or signed tokens. HMAC request signatures belong on verify_signature, not here. Secrets come from credentials, ENV, or ctx — never an inline literal. Fails with generate_token.failed.

config_fields.name: tokenType
config_fields.description: jwt: signed JWT from payloadVariable plus claims. signed: MessageVerifier cookie/link for JSON payloads (pair with verify_token signed). numeric_otp: digit code of tokenLength, e.g. email/SMS one-time codes.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key that receives the token string. Default token.

config_fields.name: tokenLength
config_fields.description: Digit count for numeric_otp (4-12). Default 6, e.g. 004821. Not a signed token.

config_fields.name: payloadVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the JWT or signed payload hash, e.g. payload. Optional for JWT (empty becomes {}). Signed payloads must be JSON-compatible.

config_fields.name: issuer
config_fields.description: Value written to the JWT iss claim, e.g. auth.example.com. Verify with verify_token verifyIssuer.

config_fields.name: audience
config_fields.description: Value written to the JWT aud claim, e.g. api.example.com. Verify with verify_token verifyAudience.

config_fields.name: subject
config_fields.description: Value written to the JWT sub claim, e.g. user-123. Prefer this over putting sub only inside payloadVariable.

config_fields.name: includeIssuedAt
config_fields.description: When true (default), write iat as Time.current.to_i. Turn off only when a caller must omit iat.

config_fields.name: notBefore
config_fields.description: Ruby expression for the nbf claim, e.g. Time.current.to_i. Leave blank to omit.

config_fields.name: expiresIn
config_fields.description: Lifetime as seconds (3600), ISO 8601 (PT1H), or a duration such as 1h. Default 1h. Empty means no expiry (avoid for JWTs).

config_fields.name: claims
config_fields.description: Extra JWT claims. Keys are identifiers; values are Ruby expressions, e.g. role => ctx[:user].role. Merged over payloadVariable.

config_fields.name: keyId
config_fields.description: Optional JWT kid header, e.g. key-2026-01, so verifiers can pick a key.

config_fields.name: algorithm
config_fields.description: JWT signing algorithm. HS256 (default), HS384, HS512 use the HMAC secret; RS256 needs a PEM RSA private key at secretVariable. none is not allowed.

config_fields.name: secretSource
config_fields.description: Where the signing secret is read. credentials: Rails credentials at secretVariable, or secret_key_base when blank. env: ENV name. ctx: ctx key. Never a literal secret.

config_fields.name: secretVariable
config_fields.description: credentials: dot path such as jwt.hmac. env: ENV name such as JWT_SECRET. ctx: identifier such as jwt_secret. Required for env and ctx.

config_fields.name: purpose
config_fields.description: MessageVerifier purpose string. Must match verify_token, e.g. flowchart_token or password_reset. A mismatch refuses the token.

step_actions.label: Hash Data
step_actions.description: Hashes sourceVariable into resultVar. Use bcrypt (default cost 12), scrypt, or argon2 to store passwords — never sha256/sha512 for passwords. Use sha256/sha512 (optional salt and pepper) for checksums, and pbkdf2 when a caller requires that KDF. MD5 and SHA-1 are not offered. Fails with hash_data.failed on Crypto::Error or PasswordHash::Error.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the value to hash, e.g. password or checksum_source.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key that receives the encoded hash string. Default hashed.

config_fields.name: algorithm
config_fields.description: bcrypt/scrypt/argon2: password hashes (self-salted). pbkdf2: HMAC-SHA256 KDF (needs salt). sha256/sha512: digests for checksums, not passwords. Default sha256.

config_fields.name: cost
config_fields.description: bcrypt cost factor (4-31). Default 12. Higher is slower; keep 10-14 on web workers.

config_fields.name: iterations
config_fields.description: pbkdf2 HMAC rounds (default 100000, max 1000000). For scrypt this maps to a time budget (100000 is about 0.2s).

config_fields.name: salt
config_fields.description: Context path of salt mixed into sha256/sha512 (prepended) or pbkdf2. Required for pbkdf2. Example: salt. bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 generate their own salt.

config_fields.name: pepper
config_fields.description: Context path of an extra secret appended to sha256/sha512 input, e.g. pepper. Not used for password algorithms or pbkdf2.

config_fields.name: encoding
config_fields.description: Digest encoding: hex (default), base64, or base64url. Ignored for bcrypt, scrypt, and argon2, which return their own encoded strings.

config_fields.name: timeCost
config_fields.description: Argon2 time cost (iterations), 1-8. Default 2.

config_fields.name: memoryCost
config_fields.description: Argon2 memory cost as log2 KiB, 8-17 (17 is 128 MiB). Default 16.

step_actions.label: Mask Data
step_actions.description: Masks sourceVariable for logs or UI and writes the display string to resultVar. Use credit_card (PCI BIN+last4), email, phone, mobile (CN 11-digit first3+last4), ssn, id_number (CN resident ID first6+last4), name, address, last4, first1_last1, or full. custom uses regexPattern or visibleStart/visibleEnd. Fails with mask_data.failed.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the value to mask, e.g. credit_card, email, or national_id.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key that receives the masked display string. Default masked.

config_fields.name: maskType
config_fields.description: Preset: last4, first1_last1, email (keep local first char + domain), phone (last4 + +CC), mobile (first3+last4), ssn (last4), credit_card (BIN+last4), id_number (first6+last4), name, address, full. custom uses regex or windows.

config_fields.name: visibleStart
config_fields.description: For custom with no regexPattern: significant characters kept at the start. Default 0. Example: 3 with visibleEnd 4 on a mobile number.

config_fields.name: visibleEnd
config_fields.description: For custom with no regexPattern: significant characters kept at the end. Default 0. Example: 4.

config_fields.name: maskChar
config_fields.description: Single character used to hide the masked portion. Default * . Example: X.

config_fields.name: preserveFormat
config_fields.description: When true (default), keep dashes/spaces on phone, mobile, ssn, credit_card, and id_number. When false, mask a digits-only (or alnum for id_number) compact form.

config_fields.name: regexPattern
config_fields.description: When set, each regex match is replaced with maskChar, e.g. \d. When blank, custom uses visibleStart/visibleEnd instead.

step_actions.label: Register member
step_actions.description: Registers a public visitor as a passwordless member on a person entity and writes {status: created|existing} to resultVar. Reads personVar (the EntityEntry) and identityVar (first_name, last_name, email). Taken emails and quota exhaustion look like existing (anti-enumeration). Use authenticate for sign-in, not this step. Fails public_only, person_entity_required, signup_disabled, or unavailable.

config_fields.name: personVar
config_fields.description: Context path of the person EntityEntry this step writes, e.g. model. Must belong to ctx[:customer_id] and the bound person entity.

config_fields.name: identityVar
config_fields.description: Context path of the identity hash with first_name, last_name, and email, e.g. identity. A taken email still succeeds as status existing.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key that receives {status: created} or {status: existing}. Default registration. Browser-visible success is the same for both.

step_actions.label: Sanitize Input
step_actions.description: Sanitizes sourceVariable HTML/text and writes the safe string to resultVar. strip_tags (default) uses Rails FullSanitizer; escape_html uses ERB::Util.html_escape for display; rails is SafeListSanitizer with allowedTags/allowedAttributes. Use this before storing or rendering visitor copy. Fails with sanitize_input.failed when onOverflow is fail.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the submitted text, e.g. user_input or comment_body.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key that receives the sanitized string. Default sanitized.

config_fields.name: sanitizer
config_fields.description: strip_tags: drop every HTML tag (Rails FullSanitizer). escape_html: escape <>& for safe display. rails: keep only allowedTags and allowedAttributes via SafeListSanitizer.

config_fields.name: allowedTags
config_fields.description: Tag names the rails sanitizer may keep, e.g. b, i, a. Empty keeps none. Letters, digits, and hyphens only.

config_fields.name: allowedAttributes
config_fields.description: Attribute names the rails sanitizer may keep, e.g. href. Empty keeps none.

config_fields.name: removeNullBytes
config_fields.description: When true (default), delete NUL bytes before sanitizing. Turn off only when a caller must preserve them.

config_fields.name: maxLength
config_fields.description: Maximum character length after sanitizing. 0 (default) means no limit. Example: 2000. onOverflow decides what happens when longer.

config_fields.name: onOverflow
config_fields.description: When maxLength is positive and the text is longer: truncate (default, String#truncate) or fail the step with sanitize_input.failed.

config_fields.name: trimWhitespace
config_fields.description: When true, strip leading and trailing whitespace after sanitizing. Default false.

step_actions.label: Verify Signature
step_actions.description: Verifies an inbound webhook HMAC (constant-time via ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils) with optional timestamp replay protection. Use this before trusting a callback body; use send_webhook to sign outbound POSTs. Reads payloadVariable, signatureVariable, and the secret from credentials (keyPath), ENV (keyPath), or ctx (secretVariable)—never a literal secret. signedPayload timestamp_body also reads timestampVariable, payloadSeparator, and toleranceSeconds (default 300). Writes resultVar (default signature_valid). onInvalid fail (default) refuses with verify_signature.invalid, expired, or missing_secret; flag stores false and continues.

config_fields.name: payloadVariable
config_fields.description: ctx path of the raw request body that was signed, e.g. raw_body. Must be the exact bytes the sender hashed.

config_fields.name: signatureVariable
config_fields.description: ctx path of the signature header or query value, e.g. params.signature or params["X-Hub-Signature-256"].

config_fields.name: secretSource
config_fields.description: Where the HMAC secret is read: credentials (Rails credentials at keyPath), env (ENV[keyPath]), or ctx (secretVariable). Never a literal secret.

config_fields.name: keyPath
config_fields.description: credentials: dot-path such as webhooks.signing_secret. env: ENV name such as WEBHOOK_SECRET. Required for credentials and env.

config_fields.name: secretVariable
config_fields.description: ctx path of the HMAC secret when secretSource is ctx, e.g. webhook_secret. Hidden for credentials/env.

config_fields.name: algorithm
config_fields.description: HMAC digest used to recompute the signature: sha256 (default), sha512, or sha1. Must match the sender.

config_fields.name: encoding
config_fields.description: How the digest is encoded before comparison: hex (default) or base64. Comparison is constant-time.

config_fields.name: signaturePrefix
config_fields.description: Prefix stripped from the header before comparison, e.g. sha256=. Blank keeps the raw header. Stripe v1= candidates are also accepted.

config_fields.name: signedPayload
config_fields.description: body (default) HMACs the payload only. timestamp_body HMACs timestamp + separator + payload and applies toleranceSeconds.

config_fields.name: timestampVariable
config_fields.description: ctx path of the timestamp included in the signed payload, e.g. params.timestamp. Unix seconds or milliseconds.

config_fields.name: payloadSeparator
config_fields.description: String inserted between timestamp and body when both are signed. Default "." (Stripe-style t.payload).

config_fields.name: toleranceSeconds
config_fields.description: Maximum age of the timestamp in seconds (0-86400). Default 300. 0 disables the replay check.

config_fields.name: onInvalid
config_fields.description: fail (default) refuses the submission with verify_signature.invalid or expired. flag stores false in resultVar and continues.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: ctx key for the boolean result (default signature_valid). true when the HMAC matches; false when onInvalid is flag and it does not.

step_actions.label: Verify Token
step_actions.description: Verifies a JWT (jwt gem, allow-listed HS*/RS256) or a Rails MessageVerifier signed payload from generate_token and writes claims to resultVar. Secrets come from credentials, ENV, or ctx — never an inline literal. Use authenticate for passwords/sessions and verify_signature for inbound HMAC webhooks. Invalid tokens fail with verify_token.failed unless onInvalid is flag (then validVar is boolean).

config_fields.name: tokenType
config_fields.description: jwt: decode and verify a JWT from generate_token jwt. signed: verify a MessageVerifier payload from generate_token signed (same purpose).

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Context path of the token string, e.g. token or auth_token.

config_fields.name: secretSource
config_fields.description: Where the verification secret is read. Must match generate_token: credentials (secretVariable or secret_key_base), env, or ctx. Never a literal secret.

config_fields.name: secretVariable
config_fields.description: credentials: dot path such as jwt.hmac. env: ENV name such as JWT_SECRET. ctx: identifier such as jwt_secret. Required for env and ctx. Blank credentials uses secret_key_base.

config_fields.name: algorithm
config_fields.description: Single allowed JWT algorithm. HS256 (default), HS384, HS512, or RS256. Must match the issuer. none is not allowed.

config_fields.name: verifyIssuer
config_fields.description: Expected JWT iss claim, e.g. https://issuer.example. Leave blank to skip iss.

config_fields.name: verifyAudience
config_fields.description: Expected JWT aud claim, e.g. api.example. Leave blank to skip aud.

config_fields.name: leewaySeconds
config_fields.description: Clock-skew leeway in seconds for exp/nbf/iat. Default 0. Example: 10.

config_fields.name: requiredClaims
config_fields.description: Claim paths that must be present. Nested keys use dots, e.g. user.role => admin. A blank value only checks presence.

config_fields.name: purpose
config_fields.description: MessageVerifier purpose. Must match generate_token, e.g. flowchart_token or password_reset.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key that receives the JWT payload hash or the signed JSON payload. Default claims. Nil when onInvalid is flag and the token is invalid.

config_fields.name: onInvalid
config_fields.description: fail: stop with verify_token.failed. flag: write resultVar (possibly nil) and validVar, then continue.

config_fields.name: validVar
config_fields.description: Ctx key set to true or false when onInvalid is flag. Default token_valid.

step_actions.label: Run background job
step_actions.description: Enqueues an allow-listed Active Job via set(queue, priority, wait, wait_until).perform_later. Use now for immediate work, at for a timestamp, after for a delay in seconds, or recurring for the next cron tick (Fugit) or a bounded burst of delayed jobs. Recurring interval times limit pre-books N delayed jobs (first after one interval); it is not a persistent scheduler, so use cron for a repeating clock. Writes resultVar with the job id (or an array of ids). Fails with enqueue_job.failed when the class is not an ApplicationJob, enqueue is aborted, or the cron/horizon is invalid.

config_fields.name: jobClass
config_fields.description: Allow-listed ApplicationJob class to run, for example ProcessOrderJob. Resolved through Invocable.job!; arbitrary constants are refused.

config_fields.name: when
config_fields.description: When to run. now enqueues immediately; at uses runAt; after waits waitSeconds; recurring uses cronExpression (next tick only) or intervalSeconds x recurrenceLimit (pre-booked delays).

config_fields.name: jobArgs
config_fields.description: Ruby expression for perform arguments, for example ctx[:order].id or ctx[:user_id], ctx[:order_id]. Leave blank for no arguments.

config_fields.name: queueName
config_fields.description: Active Job queue. default is the app queue; low and high are priority aliases; mailers is the mailer queue.

config_fields.name: priority
config_fields.description: Active Job priority from 0 to 1000. Leave blank for the adapter default.

config_fields.name: runAt
config_fields.description: Ruby time expression for when=at, for example 1.hour.from_now or Time.zone.parse(ctx[:due_at]). Clamped to the next 30 days.

config_fields.name: waitSeconds
config_fields.description: Delay in seconds for when=after, for example 3600 for one hour. Clamped to 30 days.

config_fields.name: cronExpression
config_fields.description: Five-field cron for when=recurring, for example 0 9 * * 1-5 (weekdays at 09:00). Only the next occurrence is enqueued. Takes precedence over intervalSeconds.

config_fields.name: timezone
config_fields.description: IANA timezone for the cron expression, for example UTC or America/New_York. Ignored for interval bursts.

config_fields.name: intervalSeconds
config_fields.description: Seconds between pre-booked delayed jobs when cronExpression is blank (1-86400, default 3600). First job waits one interval; this is not a persistent repeating schedule.

config_fields.name: recurrenceLimit
config_fields.description: How many delayed jobs to pre-book when cronExpression is blank (1-100, default 1). intervalSeconds x this value must stay within 30 days.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable that receives the Active Job id string, or an array of ids for an interval burst.

step_actions.label: Compress Files
step_actions.description: Zips ctx files into one archive payload {filename, content, content_type} for emailing or attaching. Map archive names to ctx variables that hold bytes or file payloads from generate_file or download_file. Use decompress_files to extract an incoming ZIP. Only ZIP is produced. Writes resultVar. Fails with compress_files.failed when there are no entries, an entry is too large, or a name is zip-slip-unsafe.

config_fields.name: entries
config_fields.description: Archive entry name mapped to a ctx variable. Example: key data.txt, value generated_file. The variable may hold raw bytes or a file payload; content is zipped under the key name.

config_fields.name: literalEntries
config_fields.description: Archive entry name mapped to literal UTF-8 text, for a static README.txt inside the ZIP. Leave empty when every entry comes from ctx.

config_fields.name: compressionLevel
config_fields.description: ZIP deflate level from 0 (store) to 9 (smallest). Leave blank for the RubyZip default.

config_fields.name: includeHidden
config_fields.description: When true, keep entry names that start with a dot, such as .env. Default skips those names.

config_fields.name: filenameTemplate
config_fields.description: ZIP filename such as orders.zip or orders-{{ "now" | date: "%Y%m%d" }}.zip. When blank, the payload filename is archive.zip.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable that receives the ZIP file payload {filename, content, content_type} for upload_file, send_email attachments, or a later download step.

step_actions.label: Decompress Files
step_actions.description: Extracts a ZIP (or an auto-detected tar/gz vendor archive) into an array of file payloads {filename, content, content_type} in resultVar. Pair with download_file or a record attachment, then bulk_import a CSV inside. Zip-slip paths and decompression bombs are refused (entry count and expanded-byte caps). Reads sourceVariable (bytes or a file payload). Fails with decompress_files.failed on a corrupt archive, path traversal, or a cap breach.

config_fields.name: sourceVariable
config_fields.description: Ctx path of the archive bytes or file payload, for example archive from download_file or compress_files. Nested paths use Step.dig.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable that receives an array of file payloads {filename, content, content_type}, one per extracted file, for upload_file or bulk_import.

config_fields.name: format
config_fields.description: Archive kind. auto sniffs ZIP (PK), gzip, or tar; zip is the usual export; tar, gz, and tar_gz accept vendor dumps that download_file fetched. Prefer auto.

config_fields.name: filter
config_fields.description: Optional fnmatch of names to keep, for example *.csv. Blank keeps every safe entry.

config_fields.name: maxEntries
config_fields.description: Maximum archive members to open (1-1000). Leave blank for the platform cap. Stops a zip bomb that lists thousands of files.

config_fields.name: maxTotalBytes
config_fields.description: Maximum expanded bytes across extracted files. Leave blank for the platform cap (100 MB).

step_actions.label: Download File
step_actions.description: Downloads a file over HTTPS from an allow-listed public URL (SSRF-blocked by OutboundHttp) into ctx as a file payload {filename, content, content_type}. Use this to fetch a vendor CSV or ZIP for bulk_import or decompress_files. Prefer urlVariable when the URL comes from a record; url is a static fallback. Writes resultVar. Optional Content-Type allow-list, SHA-256/MD5 checksum, 25 MB size cap, redirects, retries, and a circuit breaker. Fails with download_file.failed or HTTP/transport codes when the host is blocked, the type/checksum/size is wrong, or the request errors.

config_fields.name: url
config_fields.description: Static HTTPS URL to GET, for example https://files.example.com/orders.csv. Ignored when urlVariable is set and that ctx value is present. Private hosts are blocked.

config_fields.name: urlVariable
config_fields.description: Ctx path that holds the download URL, for example invoice.file_url. When set, it is tried first; url is the fallback if that path is blank.

config_fields.name: resultVar
config_fields.description: Ctx variable that receives the file payload {filename, content, content_type} for generate-file consumers such as upload_file, compress_files, or bulk_import.

config_fields.name: maxSizeBytes
config_fields.description: Reject a response larger than this many bytes (1-104857600). Default is 25 MB, hard-capped at 100 MB, streamed so an oversized body is aborted mid-transfer.

config_fields.name: followRedirects
config_fields.description: When true (default), follow HTTP redirects up to maxRedirects. Turn off to refuse any redirect.

config_fields.name: maxRedirects
config_fields.description: Maximum redirects to follow when followRedirects is on (0-10, default 3).

config_fields.name: headers
config_fields.description: Extra request headers as name/value pairs, for example Accept mapped to text/csv. Do not put secrets in the flowchart; use a ctx value only if the secret is already in ctx.

config_fields.name: allowedContentTypes
config_fields.description: Allowed response Content-Type values such as text/csv or application/zip. Empty allows any type. A mismatch fails the step.
